name: Pacific Ocean
genZNote: The Pacific is so big that Asia, the Americas AND Australia all get a coastline on it and there's still room left over. One ocean, three continents' worth of trade routes.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Extent
bullets: The largest and deepest ocean on Earth, stretching from the Arctic in the north to the Southern Ocean in the south, and from Asia/Australia in the west to the Americas in the east.
Covers roughly a third of the Earth's surface — larger than all the continents combined.
Home of the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point in any ocean.
Divided informally into the North Pacific and South Pacific by the equator.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries With Coastlines On It
bullets: East Asia: China, Japan, South Korea, North Korea, Taiwan.
Southeast Asia: Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia (through connected seas).
Oceania: Australia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Fiji, and the smaller Pacific Island nations (Samoa, Tonga, Kiribati, and others).
The Americas: the entire west coast — Canada, the United States, Mexico, and the Pacific-facing countries of Central and South America (Peru, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador).
Countries are described here as having coastlines ON the Pacific, not "surrounding" it — a more geographically careful phrasing for an ocean this size.

sections.heading: 🌐 Connected Seas & Notable Features
bullets: Major connected seas: South China Sea, East China Sea, Sea of Japan, Coral Sea, Tasman Sea, Sea of Okhotsk.
The Pacific "Ring of Fire" — a horseshoe of volcanoes and earthquake zones — runs along most of its rim.
Thousands of islands, from large ones (New Guinea, Japan's main islands) to small coral atolls across Micronesia, Melanesia and Polynesia.
The Panama Canal (see the Strait/Canal entries) links the Pacific to the Atlantic on the American side.

sections.heading: 🚢 Trade & Economic Significance
bullets: Carries the largest share of global container shipping traffic — trans-Pacific routes connect East Asian manufacturing (China, Japan, South Korea) with North American consumer markets.
Major exports moving across it: electronics, machinery, vehicles, and consumer goods from East Asia; agricultural products and raw materials from the Americas and Oceania.
Home to some of the world's busiest container ports: Shanghai, Singapore (via connected seas), Shenzhen, Busan, Los Angeles/Long Beach.
APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) is the major regional trade forum built around this ocean.

sections.heading: 🐠 Marine Ecology & Environmental Concerns
bullets: Contains the Coral Triangle (around Indonesia, the Philippines and Papua New Guinea) — the single richest marine biodiversity zone on Earth.
The Great Barrier Reef, off Australia's Coral Sea coast, is the world's largest coral reef system.
The Great Pacific Garbage Patch — a large accumulation zone of floating plastic debris between Hawaii and California — is a well-documented plastic-pollution hotspot.
Warming Pacific waters drive El Niño/La Niña cycles, which affect weather and fisheries far beyond the ocean itself.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Pacific Ocean is Earth's largest and deepest ocean, bordered by Asia, Oceania and the Americas, and central to global trans-Pacific trade.
keyFacts: Largest and deepest ocean; contains the Mariana Trench.
Bordered by East Asia, Southeast Asia, Oceania, and the Americas.
Ring of Fire runs around most of its rim.
Coral Triangle = richest marine biodiversity zone on Earth.
commonConfusion: The Pacific isn't "surrounded" by any single region — treat East Asia, Oceania and the Americas as three separate coastlines on the same ocean, not one continuous ring of countries.

highYieldFacts: Largest and deepest ocean on Earth; roughly a third of Earth's surface.
Mariana Trench — deepest known oceanic point.
Coral Triangle: Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea region.
commonTraps: Don't confuse the Ring of Fire (a seismic/volcanic zone) with a trade route or a current.
The Panama Canal connects the Pacific and Atlantic — it is a canal, not a strait (no naturally occurring channel).
mustRemember: Pacific Ocean = largest + deepest; Ring of Fire; Coral Triangle; trans-Pacific trade backbone.
